name: Due process of law
description: Due process requires government to follow fair procedures—and in substantive strands, to respect certain baseline protections—before depriving persons of life, liberty, or property (Fifth Amendment as to federal power; Fourteenth as to states).
foundationStrengthRationale: Deeply embedded in federal and state practice; central to modern rights litigation.

pros.claim: Guards against arbitrary punishment, secret proceedings, and capricious administrative action.
pros.evidence: Procedural requirements such as notice and hearing are standard features of deprivation scenarios.

cons.claim: Open-ended phrasing invites wide judicial discretion and disagreement over what process is due and what substance is protected.
cons.evidence: Long-running doctrinal splits over incorporation, fundamental rights, and administrative due process.

jurisdictions.citation: U.S. Const. amends. V, XIV, Section 1
